title: God of War Ragnarök Review
description: God of War Ragnarök review covering Kratos and Atreus, expanded combat, companions, exploration, side stories, Valhalla and the current complete package.
body:
God of War Ragnarök is both a sequel and a conclusion to the Norse arc begun by God of War (2018). It expands the number of playable spaces, companions and combat options while carrying forward the close character focus that redefined the series in the previous game.

A final Neural Critic review should judge whether that greater scale strengthens the story or crowds it, whether combat meaningfully evolves across the campaign, and how exploration balances authored spectacle with optional discovery. The current review scope also needs to account for the Valhalla expansion and the later PC version without confusing those additions with the original 2022 launch package.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Official God of War Ragnarök promotional artwork used as the review feature image.

cons: Pacing is uneven in several stretches
The final escalation can feel rushed relative to the buildup
reviewMeta.verdict: An ambitious sequel with richer combat, superb performances and excellent character work that sometimes struggles under the weight of its own scope.

contentBlocks.text:
Ragnarök expands from a family story into a conflict involving more realms, factions and mythological figures. Kratos and Atreus remain the emotional center, but the narrative regularly shifts attention toward a larger ensemble.

That broader scope gives the sequel more perspectives and relationships to develop while creating a constant tension between intimate character work and large-scale mythic stakes.
contentBlocks.heading: The Story Balances Intimacy With a Much Larger Conflict

contentBlocks.text:
The combat system retains the close over-the-shoulder structure of God of War (2018) while expanding abilities, equipment choices and encounter variety. Different tools and companion actions create more tactical decisions across a longer campaign.

The added complexity gives players more ways to shape encounters, although the interface and progression systems also have more information to communicate than before.
contentBlocks.heading: Combat Adds Options Without Replacing the 2018 Foundation

contentBlocks.text:
Ragnarök gives companion characters a larger mechanical and narrative role. Their presence affects conversations, puzzle interactions and combat support, while the story repeatedly changes who is traveling with the player.

That rotation makes the journey more dynamic and lets relationships develop through ordinary exploration as well as major story scenes.
contentBlocks.heading: Companions Change the Rhythm of Encounters and Exploration

contentBlocks.text:
The game presents interconnected regions with optional paths, side stories and revisitable spaces rather than one seamless open map. Some realms are tightly directed while others open into larger hubs.

The structure supports exploration without abandoning the authored pacing of the main story, though the urgency of the narrative can sometimes sit awkwardly beside long optional detours.
contentBlocks.heading: The Nine Realms Are Broader, but Not a Conventional Open World

contentBlocks.text:
Optional quests frequently focus on companions, local history and consequences of earlier events rather than functioning only as reward delivery. That gives side content an unusually large role in expanding relationships and world context.

Several of the game’s most useful character moments live outside the direct critical path, which makes exploration part of the narrative experience rather than a separate checklist layer.
contentBlocks.heading: Side Stories Are Important to the Character Work

contentBlocks.text:
The no-cut camera approach continues from God of War (2018), keeping conversations, exploration and major story moments within a continuous visual grammar. That creates immediacy and keeps transitions closely tied to the player’s perspective.

The technique is more demanding in a larger sequel because it has to carry more locations, characters and pacing changes without relying on conventional cinematic cuts.
contentBlocks.heading: Presentation Still Depends on the Continuous-Camera Style

contentBlocks.text:
God of War Ragnarök: Valhalla is a free post-launch expansion that continues character work after the main story through a repeatable structure. It is included with the PC version alongside other post-launch updates.

Valhalla is discussed as part of the current complete God of War Ragnarök package.
contentBlocks.heading: Valhalla Extends the Character Arc After the Main Game

contentBlocks.text:
God of War Ragnarök launched on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 in November 2022 and arrived on PC on September 19, 2024. The PC release includes Valhalla and post-launch updates, while technical options differ across versions.

Performance, image quality, input features and loading observations refer to the PC version available through Steam.
contentBlocks.heading: Current Platform Context

quickRead: The sequel expands the 2018 foundation with more realms, characters and combat options.
Kratos and Atreus remain the emotional center even as the story broadens to a larger ensemble.
Optional quests carry important character work and make exploration more meaningful than simple map completion.
Valhalla changes the modern package, so the final review scope should state whether it is included in the score.
conclusion:
God of War Ragnarök expands nearly every part of the 2018 foundation: more realms, more characters, broader side stories and more combat options. Its central strength remains the relationship-driven story around Kratos and Atreus, while the larger scale creates a constant tradeoff between intimacy and momentum.\n\nValhalla strengthens the current package with a focused post-game character arc. The 9.1 verdict reflects the PC version reviewed through Steam.
